chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the New York City Council vote, asks everyone to silence phones, and instructs that no one approach the dais before inviting the chair to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff opens the hearing and sets protocol

utterances.text: Hello, good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to today's New York City Council vote.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please silence all phones.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Moving forward, no one is to approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, you may begin.

chapters.summary: Council Member Pierina Ana Sanchez identifies herself as chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings and announces that the committee will vote on proposed Intro 1015-A to improve and extend the J-51 tax abatement program.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez convenes Housing and Buildings vote on Intro 1015-A

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Sergeants, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Pierina Sanchez, Chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, the committee will be voting on proposed intro number 1015A, a bill to improve and extend the J51 tax abatement program.

chapters.summary: Sanchez says aging New York City buildings are at the center of both the housing and climate crises, citing failing elevators, stranded seniors and disabled residents, roof boilers, electrical systems, and deadly fire hazards in the Bronx and Queens. She argues government must set safety standards while helping owners make needed investments.
chapters.title: Sanchez frames J-51 vote as response to housing and climate crises

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: New York City is facing a housing crisis and a climate crisis, and our aging buildings are at the center of both.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Our buildings are among the largest sources of greenhouse gas emissions, even as they break down around us.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Elevators are failing, stranding seniors and people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Roof boilers and electrical systems and other critical infrastructures need investment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And in the Bronx and Queens, we are living the deadly consequences of aging, housing, and fire hazards.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: While government has a responsibility to set high standards for owners to keep buildings safe, protect tenants, and reduce emissions, we must also help owners to make the investments being asked of them.

chapters.summary: Sanchez says Intro 1015-A would improve and extend J-51, a tax abatement for eligible multifamily housing including rentals, co-ops, and condos. She calls it a key tool for preservation, energy efficiency, and Local Law 97 compliance, noting the city dedicated $212.7 million to J-51 in fiscal year 2026.
chapters.title: Sanchez explains J-51 tax abatement purpose and $212.7 million cost

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, I am proud that the Council will be voting on 1015A, which will do just that by improving and

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: extending the J51 tax abatement program.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: J51 offers a tax abatement for eligible multifamily housing, including certain rental buildings, co-ops, and condos.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: It's one of the city's most important financial tools for helping owners to keep up with the cost necessary to preserve and upgrade their properties, including energy efficiency work, so that buildings can better comply with local law 97.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And this is not a small program.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The mayor's report on tax expenditures reports that the city dedicated $212.7 million to the J51 program in the 2026 fiscal year.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That's foregone tax expenditures in service of improving old properties.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This program enables building owners to replace elevators, wheelchair lifts, repair roofing, install energy-efficient equipment, and J51 is only becoming more essential as older buildings continue to deteriorate and

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: climate change continues to require urgent action.

chapters.summary: Sanchez outlines the bill's three key changes: a 10-year extension for projects completed between June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2036; an increase from 80% to 100% recovery of reasonable rehabilitation costs; and a co-op/condo assessed valuation cap increase from $45,000 to $60,000 per unit, indexed to inflation. She says the program could reach over 300,000 co-op and condo units.
chapters.title: Sanchez details three state-authorized changes in Intro 1015-A

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Earlier this year, New York State authorized the city to extend J51 and made three key changes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: First, the legislation will provide a longer extension than previous reauthorizations.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: If passed today, 1015A will extend J51 for 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This means eligible projects that are complete between June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2036, when I will finally be 21 years old, just kidding, are able to receive this tax benefit.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Second,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Under 1015A, building owners would now be able to recover up to 100% of the reasonable cost of their rehabilitation work.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: It used to be 80%.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And third, for co-ops and condos, this bill raises the assessed valuation cap from $45,000 per unit to $60,000 per unit and will be updated regularly to account for inflation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: With these changes, the program has the potential to reach more than 300,000 co-ops and condo units citywide.

chapters.summary: Sanchez says Intro 1015-A maintains accountability mechanisms for terminating or revoking benefits, including the affidavit of no harassment. She adds that the Council is adding comprehensive reporting on which buildings receive J-51, how much they receive, work categories, locations, and rental versus homeownership breakdowns.
chapters.title: Sanchez highlights J-51 accountability and new reporting requirements

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And in addition to these changes, 1015A will maintain previous accountability mechanisms for terminating or revoking the benefits if any building fails to comply with the program requirements, including the affidavit of no harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The council is also adding comprehensive reporting on which buildings receive the new J51 benefit, how much they receive, the categories of work they are pursuing, where they are located, and the breakdown between rental and homeownership buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This will provide the public with transparent information on how the city is using its resources and help to shape future iterations of the J51 program.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks the Green Co-op Council, State Senator Brian Kavanaugh, committee staff including Austin Malone, Billy Eck, Jose Conde, Dirk Spencer, Carla Naranjo, Mohamed Shadid, and Noah Slosberg, and her personal team. She gives a special farewell shout-out to legislative fellow Dylan Campos in his last stated meeting with the team.
chapters.title: Sanchez thanks J-51 advocates, staff, and departing fellow Dylan Campos

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, the thank yous.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: First, I want to thank the Green Co-op Council for their persistent advocacy and State Senator Brian Kavanaugh, the Chair of Housing in the Senate, for his leadership on this issue in the legislature.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: To the Housing and Buildings Committee staff, Senior Legislative Council Austin Malone, Legislative Council Billy Eck, Senior Policy Analyst Jose Conde, Senior Policy Analyst...

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Dirk Spencer, finance analyst Carla.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Naranjo, and data scientist Mohamed Shadid, and Noah Slosberg.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And last but not least, my team, Deputy Chiefs of Staff Ben Ratner and Kim Castellanos, District Director Maria Jose Mares, Gerard Fernandez, Oriana Roa Acevedo, Soraya Bonilla, Marcus Kahn, and Jacob Hayward.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I want to take this moment to send a very special shout out to Dylan Campos, our incredible legislative fellow, and who for today, this will be his last stated meeting with us.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We're just so lucky to have had you on our team.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You got us out of quite a few pickles and past, you know, some really important moments.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much for everything you did for this team.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You will always be a part of Team Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And I'm joined today by my colleagues, but I'll turn it over to the clerk to call the roll.

summary: Committee on Housing and Buildings holds a roll-call vote on proposed Intro 1015-A to improve and extend the J-51 tax abatement program.

Chair Pierina Ana Sanchez explains the bill's housing and climate rationale, 10-year extension, 100% rehabilitation cost recovery, higher co-op/condo valuation cap, and new accountability and reporting requirements.
The committee votes 11-0 to adopt Intro 1015-A, with members congratulating the chair, and the hearing adjourns.
title: Committee on Housing and Buildings
topic: Abatement of taxation for alterations and improvements to certain multiple dwellings
